paper_title: Searching for solar axions using data from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory
notes: Paper excludes the isovector coupling |g3_aN| = |g_an-g_ap|/2 > 2e-5 GeV^-1 at 95% CL for sub-MeV masses (exclusion band 2e-5 to 1e-3 GeV^-1, solar-trapping upper bound ~1e-3 GeV^-1 not reported here; lower boundary is the headline curve). Curve digitised from the vector paths of Fig. 1 (blue SNO region, file AxionLimitsv2.pdf in the e-print): flat at g3=10^-4.697=2.0e-5 GeV^-1, rising above ~1 MeV; the figure frame clips at 3.2 MeV although the text quotes sensitivity up to ~5.5 MeV (deuteron-dissociation kinematics). Per convention, reported on the single canonical neutron coupling with g_ap=0: paper Lagrangian L=(1/2) g_an (da) nbar gamma gamma5 n with g_an in GeV^-1 and g_an=2*g3 when g_ap=0, so dimensionless g_an = m_n * g_an[GeV^-1] = 2 m_n g3 (m_n=0.9396 GeV), giving flat g_an = 3.78e-5. Solar axion flux from p+d->3He+a; limit does not depend on dark matter density.
